about: Shared reference data for the switch skill, read on demand: only when the rights switch is on or offered, or when the author says yes to the offer of references. Own wording; sources are named with public links, never quoted at length. A card is a reference, not a verdict.

glossary.meaning: Every person has the same inherent worth, which no law, authority or private party may violate.
glossary.meaning_hu: Minden embernek ugyanaz a veleszületett értéke, amelyet sem törvény, sem hatóság, sem magánszemély nem sérthet meg.
glossary.binds: The state and EU institutions; private persons through the laws that protect it
glossary.limits: Not subject to weighing away: other rights may be limited, the core of dignity may not; it is no licence to restrict lawful conduct only because someone finds it offensive
common_misreadings: Used as an absolute trump to silence any view a speaker finds offensive
Treated as optional for people of a disliked group or opinion
Equated with a feeling of being insulted rather than with the worth of the person

glossary.term: Equality before the law and non-discrimination
glossary.term_hu: Törvény előtti egyenlőség és megkülönböztetés tilalma
glossary.meaning: Everyone is treated alike by the law, and differences in treatment need an objective, proportionate reason.
glossary.meaning_hu: A törvény mindenkire egyformán vonatkozik, a különbségtételhez objektív és arányos indok kell.
glossary.binds: The state and EU institutions; employers and service providers under equality statutes
glossary.limits: Differences in treatment are lawful where justified by a legitimate aim and proportionate; positive measures to remedy disadvantage can be lawful
common_misreadings: Read as requiring identical treatment even where situations differ in a relevant way
Read as allowing unequal treatment of a group because its members share a view
Invoked for one group only while the same claim by another group is dismissed

glossary.meaning: A person charged with a crime is treated as innocent until guilt is established by a court under law.
glossary.meaning_hu: A bűncselekménnyel vádolt személyt mindaddig ártatlannak kell tekinteni, amíg bíróság a törvény szerint nem állapítja meg a bűnösségét.
glossary.binds: Courts, prosecutors and public authorities in how they speak and act; the press and private persons are bound by ethics and defamation law, not by this rule as such
glossary.limits: Does not forbid reporting that a charge exists or discussing a case; it forbids officials presenting the person as guilty before judgment
common_misreadings: Read as banning the press from reporting a suspicion or charge
Read as proof that the accused did nothing, rather than a rule about treatment and burden of proof
Ignored when an authority or a crowd treats a suspect as already guilty

glossary.term: Fair trial and right of defence
glossary.term_hu: Tisztességes eljárás és védelemhez való jog
glossary.meaning: Anyone facing a charge or a civil claim gets a hearing by an independent court, with time, information and a lawyer to defend themselves.
glossary.meaning_hu: Aki ellen vádat vagy polgári igényt emelnek, azt független bíróság hallgatja meg, és van ideje, tájékoztatása és védője a védekezéshez.
glossary.holder: Every person charged or party to a case
glossary.binds: Courts, prosecutors, police and the state
glossary.limits: Some elements, such as public hearing or access to the file, can be limited for defined reasons if the whole procedure stays fair
common_misreadings: Seen as a technicality that protects only the guilty
Claimed as violated simply because the outcome was unwelcome
Reduced to the right to a lawyer while ignoring timely information and equal treatment of the parties

glossary.term_hu: Nullum crimen, nulla poena sine lege
glossary.meaning: No one is punished for something that was not a crime when it was done, and the penalty may not be heavier than the one then set.
glossary.meaning_hu: Senkit nem lehet olyan cselekményért büntetni, amely elkövetésekor nem volt bűncselekmény, és a büntetés nem lehet súlyosabb az akkor megállapítottnál.
glossary.binds: Legislators, courts and prosecutors
glossary.limits: Acts criminal under general principles of law recognised by nations remain punishable; milder later law applies
common_misreadings: Read as meaning a harmful act may never be penalised because no rule named it exactly
Applied backwards to deny that a new, milder rule helps an earlier offender
Invoked about civil or political consequences that are not criminal penalties

glossary.term: Liberty and security of the person
glossary.meaning: No one is deprived of liberty except in cases and by a procedure set by law, with a court able to review it promptly.
glossary.meaning_hu: Senkitől nem lehet elvenni a szabadságát, csak törvényben meghatározott esetben és eljárásban, és ezt bíróságnak gyorsan felül kell tudnia vizsgálni.
glossary.binds: The state: police, prosecutors, courts, detention facilities
glossary.limits: Lawful detention exists (after conviction, on reasonable suspicion, for defined protective reasons) but must be necessary, proportionate and reviewed
common_misreadings: Read as forbidding all pre-trial custody
Read as allowing custody to punish before judgment or to obtain cooperation
Claimed as violated without regard to the grounds the court gave

glossary.meaning: Everyone may hold opinions and share and receive information and ideas without interference by public authorities.
glossary.meaning_hu: Mindenki szabadon vallhat véleményt, és közölhet vagy kaphat információt és gondolatot hatósági beavatkozás nélkül.
glossary.binds: Primarily the state; private platforms and employers are bound by it only through law and contract
glossary.limits: Limits must be set by law, pursue a legitimate aim (e.g. others' reputation, public order, protection of minors) and be necessary and proportionate to that aim; incitement to violence, threats and unlawful harassment are not protected
common_misreadings: Read as a right to be free of criticism or of private moderation decisions
Read as covering threats, incitement or harassment without limit
Stated as absolute by one side and as dispensable for opinions it dislikes by the other

glossary.meaning: The press and other media may report and comment independently, and the state must respect and protect a variety of sources and views.
glossary.meaning_hu: A sajtó és a többi média függetlenül tudósíthat és véleményezhet, az államnak pedig tiszteletben kell tartania és védenie kell a források és nézetek sokféleségét.
glossary.holder: Journalists, media outlets and the public
glossary.binds: The state and EU institutions
glossary.limits: Media remain bound by defamation, privacy and accuracy duties; protection of sources is strong but not unlimited
common_misreadings: Read as immunity from any correction or legal liability
Read as the state's right to decide what counts as balanced coverage
Used to treat any criticism of an outlet as an attack on press freedom

glossary.meaning: People may meet peacefully and form or join groups, parties and unions.
glossary.meaning_hu: Az emberek békésen gyűlhetnek össze, és szabadon alapíthatnak vagy csatlakozhatnak csoportokhoz, pártokhoz, szakszervezetekhez.
glossary.binds: The state
glossary.limits: Limits for public safety, order and others' rights if necessary and proportionate; the assembly must be peaceful
common_misreadings: Read as a right to block others' movement or rights without limit
Read as a right of the authorities to ban gatherings whenever opinions displease
Applied to a group's views while the same measure is denied to the opposite group

glossary.term: Freedom of thought, conscience and religion
glossary.meaning: Everyone may hold, change and (within limits) live out their beliefs, religious or not, alone or with others.
glossary.meaning_hu: Mindenki szabadon vallhat, változtathat és (korlátok között) élhet is meggyőződése szerint, vallásos vagy más, egyedül vagy másokkal.
glossary.binds: The state; the inner belief is absolute, outward practice may be limited
glossary.limits: Manifesting a belief may be limited by law where necessary for safety, health, order or others' rights
common_misreadings: Read as exempting believers from any general law
Read as licence to treat a belief as automatically suspect or backward
Used for one tradition's practices while another's are called extremist

glossary.meaning: Everyone's private and family life, home, communications and personal data are protected from unlawful or arbitrary intrusion.
glossary.meaning_hu: Mindenki magán- és családi élete, otthona, levelezése és személyes adatai védettek a jogellenes vagy önkényes beavatkozástól.
glossary.binds: The state; private bodies through data-protection law
glossary.limits: Interference is lawful if set by law, necessary and proportionate; the private sphere of public figures is narrower where the matter is of public interest
common_misreadings: Read as banning any public mention of a named person
Read as barring all surveillance or data use, including lawful and proportionate ones
Stretched to shield matters of real public interest from reporting

glossary.meaning: Children are rights-holders: their best interests come first in decisions about them, they are protected from harm, and they may be heard in line with age and maturity.
glossary.meaning_hu: A gyermek jogok alanya: a döntéseknél elsődleges a mindenek felett álló érdeke, védelmet kap a bántalmazással szemben, és életkorához és érettségéhez mérten meghallgatandó.
glossary.binds: The state, courts, schools and carers; parents are bound in exercising their responsibility
glossary.limits: Parental guidance is lawful and expected; the child's growing capacity increases weight of their views; abuse, neglect and exploitation are crimes and never covered
common_misreadings: Invoked to override parents' lawful role where no harm or legal ground is shown
Invoked to dismiss the child's own views or access to age-appropriate information
Cited for one side of a dispute while ignoring the counterpart duties of the other

glossary.term: Parents' right to educate in line with their convictions
glossary.term_hu: A szülők joga a gyermek neveléséhez saját meggyőződésük szerint
glossary.meaning: Parents have the primary responsibility for their children's upbringing, and the state must respect their religious and philosophical convictions in education.
glossary.meaning_hu: A szülőké a gyermek nevelésének elsődleges felelőssége, az államnak pedig az oktatásban tiszteletben kell tartania vallási és világnézeti meggyőződésüket.
glossary.binds: The state in its educational functions
glossary.limits: The state sets curricula by law; parents' convictions are respected within the limits courts have drawn; a specific curriculum dispute is judged case by case under the jurisdiction rule
common_misreadings: Read as a right to veto any lawful curriculum content
Read as meaning parents' convictions never count in school matters
Used to presume parents harmful or, in the other direction, the state's teaching harmful, without grounds

glossary.meaning: Everyone has the right to education and to access to vocational training, and the state must provide it without discrimination.
glossary.meaning_hu: Mindenkinek joga van az oktatáshoz és a szakképzéshez való hozzáféréshez, és az államnak ezt megkülönböztetés nélkül kell biztosítania.
glossary.binds: The state, which organises and supervises schooling
glossary.limits: The state may regulate schools and curricula within limits of pluralism; the right does not require a particular school type
common_misreadings: Read as a right to any particular school or content of one's choosing
Read as satisfied by access alone, ignoring quality and non-discrimination
Used in one direction only, for either state or family claims

glossary.term: Free elections: the right to vote and to stand
glossary.meaning: Citizens vote by secret ballot at regular elections and may stand as candidates, so that the people can choose the legislature.
glossary.meaning_hu: Az állampolgárok rendszeres választásokon titkos szavazással szavaznak, és jelöltként indulhatnak, így a nép választja a törvényhozást.
glossary.holder: Eligible citizens and residents as set by law
glossary.binds: The state in organising elections
glossary.limits: Age, residence and similar conditions may be set if reasonable and non-arbitrary; blanket exclusions need strong justification
common_misreadings: Read as meaning the winner may disregard all minority views
Read as meaning any restriction on candidacy is illegitimate
Used to dispute results or rules by one camp that it accepts when it wins

glossary.term: Parliamentary mandate and the speech of representatives
glossary.term_hu: A képviselői megbízatás és a képviselők szólásszabadsága
glossary.meaning: An elected representative speaks and votes for the voters, with wide room to speak in the chamber and limited protection from legal action for those words.
glossary.meaning_hu: A megválasztott képviselő a választók nevében szól és szavaz, a testületben tág teret kap a felszólalásra, és az itt elmondottak miatt korlátozott jogi védelmet élvez.
glossary.holder: Members of parliament, and through them their voters
glossary.binds: Other state bodies; members themselves remain bound by chamber rules and by criminal law outside the protected scope
glossary.limits: Immunity covers opinions and votes in the performance of the mandate, not unrelated conduct; abusive or unlawful speech may be sanctioned by chamber rules
common_misreadings: Read as impunity for any act or statement of a member
Read as meaning a member may be silenced for an opinion disliked by the majority
Applied to members of one party while the other side's members are held to a different standard

glossary.meaning: Public bodies handle a person's affairs impartially, fairly and within a reasonable time, hear the person before an adverse measure, and give reasons.
glossary.meaning_hu: A hatóságok a személy ügyét pártatlanul, tisztességesen és ésszerű időn belül intézik, hátrányos intézkedés előtt meghallgatják, és indokolnak.
glossary.holder: Every person dealing with EU institutions (and, by national law, national authorities)
glossary.binds: EU institutions, bodies and agencies; national authorities under national law and EU law where it applies
glossary.limits: Charter text addresses EU bodies directly; national authorities are bound by the general principles of EU law when applying it
common_misreadings: Read as a right to the decision one wants
Read as requiring a hearing for every routine act regardless of effect
Claimed against private bodies that it does not bind

glossary.meaning: Citizens may read documents held by public institutions, unless a defined exception such as security or privacy applies.
glossary.meaning_hu: A polgárok megismerhetik a közintézmények birtokában lévő dokumentumokat, kivéve ha meghatározott kivétel, például biztonság vagy magánélet védelme áll fenn.
glossary.binds: EU institutions; national bodies under national law
glossary.limits: Exceptions (security, privacy, commercial interests, ongoing decisions) are read narrowly and weighed against public interest
common_misreadings: Read as a right to everything the authority holds
Read as meaning any refusal proves concealment
Used selectively, demanding openness from one side only

glossary.term: Effective remedy and access to a court
glossary.term_hu: Hatékony jogorvoslat és bírósághoz fordulás joga
glossary.meaning: Anyone whose rights are violated can challenge it before an independent and impartial court that can give a real remedy.
glossary.meaning_hu: Akinek a jogát megsértik, az független és pártatlan bíróság előtt vitathatja, amely valódi jogorvoslatot adhat.
glossary.binds: Member states and EU institutions in setting up courts and procedures
glossary.limits: Reasonable time limits and admissibility rules are lawful if they do not make the right illusory
common_misreadings: Read as a guarantee that the court will rule in one's favour
Read as satisfied by a nominal procedure with no power to change the outcome
Cited for one's own claims and denied to opponents

glossary.term: Separation of powers and judicial independence
glossary.term_hu: Hatalmi ágak szétválasztása és bírói függetlenség
glossary.meaning: Legislative, executive and judicial power are held apart, and judges decide cases free of pressure from the other branches or the parties.
glossary.meaning_hu: A törvényhozó, végrehajtó és bírói hatalom elkülönül, a bírák pedig a többi hatalmi ágtól és a felektől befolyásmentesen döntenek.
glossary.holder: Citizens and litigants, through the court system
glossary.binds: The state, all branches
glossary.limits: Judges remain accountable through reasoning, appeal and disciplinary procedures set by law
common_misreadings: Read as meaning judges may never be criticised
Read as meaning any unfavourable judgment proves bias or interference
Applied to courts when they rule against one camp and ignored when they rule against the other

glossary.term: Rule of law: legality and legal certainty
glossary.meaning: Public power acts only on the basis of law that is clear, public and applied equally, with no arbitrary decisions and review by courts.
glossary.meaning_hu: A közhatalom csak világos, nyilvános és mindenkire egyformán alkalmazott jogszabály alapján jár el, önkényes döntés nélkül, bírói felülvizsgálattal.
glossary.binds: All public bodies, legislators included
glossary.limits: Law may change; retroactive burdens, vague rules and unchecked discretion are what the principle resists
common_misreadings: Read as meaning every law is acceptable once enacted
Read as a one-sided charge against opponents' acts while one's own are exempt
Treated as a slogan rather than tested against legality, certainty and review

glossary.term: Prohibition of torture and degrading treatment
glossary.term_hu: A kínzás és megalázó bánásmód tilalma
glossary.meaning: No one may be tortured or subjected to inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment, in any circumstance.
glossary.meaning_hu: Senkit nem lehet kínozni, sem embertelen vagy megalázó bánásmódnak vagy büntetésnek alávetni, semmilyen körülmények között.
glossary.holder: Every person, including suspects and prisoners
glossary.binds: The state and its agents, without exception
glossary.limits: Absolute: no limit, no balancing; the dividing line (severity threshold) is a matter for the courts
common_misreadings: Read as covering any discomfort of lawful custody
Read as allowed for 'bad people' or in emergencies
Invoked for one side's detainees while the same conditions for others are ignored

glossary.meaning: People belonging to national or other minorities enjoy the same rights as everyone and may keep and develop their culture, language and religion.
glossary.meaning_hu: A nemzeti és más kisebbségekhez tartozók mindenki mással azonos jogokat élveznek, és megőrizhetik és fejleszthetik kultúrájukat, nyelvüket és vallásukat.
glossary.holder: Persons belonging to minorities (individually and with others)
glossary.binds: The state
glossary.limits: Rights are exercised within the law and with respect for others' rights
common_misreadings: Read as a claim to special treatment beyond equality
Read as meaning a minority's claims never deserve consideration
Used for one minority while another's equal claim is dismissed

glossary.meaning: Everyone may enjoy their lawfully acquired possessions; a person may be deprived of property only in the public interest, by law and with fair compensation.
glossary.meaning_hu: Mindenki háborítatlanul birtokolhatja törvényesen szerzett vagyonát; tulajdonától csak közérdekből, törvény alapján és igazságos kártalanítással fosztható meg.
glossary.binds: The state
glossary.limits: The state may regulate use of property in the general interest and collect taxes; deprivation needs law, public interest and compensation
common_misreadings: Read as freedom from any regulation or taxation
Read as no protection when the owner is unpopular
Cited for one owner while the same measure is accepted against another

findings.explain: Debate is treated as valuable: a differing opinion is a chance to learn, not a threat to be removed. A text that calls disagreement itself harmful leaves no room for argument.
findings.legit_form: Firm criticism of a specific claim, which is itself part of debate.
findings.how_to_respond_fairly: Answer the claim, and say that disagreeing is welcome.

findings.explain: The argument is answered, not the person who makes it. Remarks on the speaker's character or background replace a reply that was owed.
findings.legit_form: Pointing out a documented conflict of interest that bears directly on a claim.
findings.how_to_respond_fairly: Restate the argument and answer that; leave the speaker out.

findings.explain: The other party is a debate partner, not an enemy. Enemy language makes listening and compromise look like betrayal.
findings.legit_form: Naming a real, lawful conflict of interests between two parties.
findings.how_to_respond_fairly: Name the disagreement without casting the other side as an enemy.

findings.explain: Understanding comes first: the text shows it has grasped the other position before replying. Answering a claim nobody made, or skipping a point, breaks this.
findings.legit_form: A short reply that quotes the point it answers.
findings.how_to_respond_fairly: Quote the other's point, check you read it right, then reply.

findings.explain: The aim is understanding, not conversion. A text that only seeks to win over, or to make the other give in, misses this.
findings.legit_form: Making a strong, honest case for one's own view.
findings.how_to_respond_fairly: State your case and ask what would change the other side's mind.

findings.explain: Sincere convictions are respected and not forced on others. Mockery of a belief, or pressure to give it up, breaks this.
findings.legit_form: Disagreeing with a conviction, and giving reasons.
findings.how_to_respond_fairly: Argue the reasons, not the believer; leave the conviction its dignity.

findings.explain: Arguments, not force, decide a debate. Volume, mockery or mass pressure replace reasons with pressure.
findings.legit_form: Strong emphasis or humour that still carries an argument.
findings.how_to_respond_fairly: Reply to the content in plain words and skip the escalation.

findings.explain: Being wrong is allowed. A text that admits no error, or punishes the other for one, shuts down learning.
findings.legit_form: Holding a position firmly while open to evidence.
findings.how_to_respond_fairly: Say what would change your mind, and credit the other's correction.

findings.explain: Every person keeps their dignity, whatever their opinion. Humiliation is not an argument and is not justified by a view.
findings.legit_form: Sharp but factual criticism of conduct.
findings.how_to_respond_fairly: Keep the criticism factual and remove wording that demeans the person.

findings.explain: We answer for what we pass on: sharing a claim, quote or post makes it ours. Repeating an unchecked item shifts the cost onto its target.
findings.legit_form: Sharing with a clear note that the item is unverified or disputed.
findings.how_to_respond_fairly: Check before sharing, and say what you did and did not verify.

findings.explain: A fair method states the other side accurately, with no strawmen and no one-sided picking of evidence.
findings.legit_form: A short summary of the other side that they would recognise.
findings.how_to_respond_fairly: Restate their view the way they would, then answer that version.

findings.explain: Plain words and honest evidence: loaded terms are avoided and no claim is stronger than its evidence. Emotive labels and overstatement break this.
findings.legit_form: A vivid but accurate description backed by evidence.
findings.how_to_respond_fairly: Swap the loaded term for a neutral one and say what the evidence shows.

findings.explain: Deflection moves the topic to what the other side did, so the original question is never answered. It matters because the point at issue is lost.
findings.legit_form: Raising a real inconsistency that bears on the same question.
findings.how_to_respond_fairly: Name the original question and answer or ask it again.

findings.explain: Shifting blame puts one's own fault on the other party. It matters because responsibility is moved away from where the facts put it.
findings.legit_form: Pointing out a real, documented share of responsibility.
findings.how_to_respond_fairly: Set out who did what with dates and sources.

findings.explain: DARVO runs Deny, Attack, Reverse Victim and Offender: the accusation is denied, the accuser attacked, and the speaker presented as the wronged party. It matters because the original claim is never examined.
findings.legit_form: Honest denial of a false accusation, or a real counter-complaint made on the facts.
findings.how_to_respond_fairly: Return to the original claim and ask for the facts on it.

findings.explain: Character assassination attacks someone's credibility instead of their argument. It matters because a claim stands or falls on its content.
findings.legit_form: Showing, with evidence, that a source has a verified record of unreliability on this very point.
findings.how_to_respond_fairly: Restate the argument and answer it on its merits.

findings.explain: Flooding sends so many claims that none can be answered in time. It matters because unanswered items can look like conceded ones.
findings.legit_form: A long, well-organised document that lists sources for each point.
findings.how_to_respond_fairly: Pick the one or two strongest points and answer only those, saying so.

findings.explain: A background campaign enlists others to apply pressure, away from the open exchange. It matters because the pressure, not the argument, decides the outcome.
findings.legit_form: Openly asking supporters to read and comment on a position.
findings.how_to_respond_fairly: Move the exchange back to the open channel and the original question.

refs_free.name: First Draft: Fake news, it's complicated

findings.explain: A tactical retreat is a show of reconciliation that draws the other party back before the pressure resumes. It matters because trust is used against the person who gave it.
findings.legit_form: A real change of position that holds in later behaviour.
findings.how_to_respond_fairly: Ask for the concrete commitment and check it against later conduct.

refs_free.name: First Draft: Fake news, it's complicated

findings.explain: Official pressure threatens reports to authorities, or exposure, to force a result. It matters because it substitutes threat for reasons and may itself breach the law.
findings.legit_form: Notifying an authority of a genuine legal breach, said openly.
findings.how_to_respond_fairly: Keep a record, stay on the argument, and seek legal or professional advice.

findings.explain: Astroturfing is commissioned opinion presented as spontaneous crowd opinion: fake profiles or organised comments make a few look like many. It matters because the apparent size of support is not real.
findings.legit_form: A genuine campaign by identified supporters, open about who runs it.
findings.how_to_respond_fairly: Check the accounts and the source before inferring any real level of support.

refs_free.name: First Draft: Fake news, it's complicated

findings.explain: A strawman argues against a distorted, easier version of the other side's view. It matters because the actual position goes unanswered.
findings.legit_form: A fair summary of a position, followed by a real critique.
findings.how_to_respond_fairly: Quote what was actually said and point to the difference.

findings.explain: Gaslighting denies that something happened, or makes the other party doubt their own memory. It matters because the person is led to distrust what they know.
findings.legit_form: A genuine, evidence-based difference over what happened.
findings.how_to_respond_fairly: Record dates and sources and compare them with the claim.

refs_free.name: First Draft: Fake news, it's complicated

findings.explain: A false dilemma offers two options when more exist. It matters because the real choice is hidden.
findings.legit_form: Naming two options that really are the only two, or the two main ones, with the others set aside openly.
findings.how_to_respond_fairly: Name the options left out.

findings.explain: A false analogy treats two different situations as alike. It matters because conclusions that fit the first case are carried over to the second without a shared basis.
findings.legit_form: A comparison that names the specific features the two cases share.
findings.how_to_respond_fairly: Point to the relevant difference between the cases.

findings.explain: A loaded question puts an accusation inside a question so any direct answer accepts it. It matters because the premise is never examined.
findings.legit_form: A question about something already established.
findings.how_to_respond_fairly: Reject or restate the premise before answering.

findings.explain: Attributed motive claims to know why someone acts, without showing it. It matters because the stated motive cannot be checked and replaces the argument.
findings.legit_form: Citing a stated purpose, or a documented interest tied to the claim.
findings.how_to_respond_fairly: Ask for what shows the motive, or answer the act itself.

findings.explain: Generalization attributes one view or act to a whole group. It matters because individuals are charged for what others said or did.
findings.legit_form: A statement of a documented, measured share of a group, with the figure.
findings.how_to_respond_fairly: Ask how many, and name the individual who said it.

findings.explain: Loaded language or euphemism frames an issue with emotive or softened words. It matters because the word decides the reader's view before the facts do.
findings.legit_form: A strong word that is accurate and defined.

techniques.name: Rights-term misuse
techniques.definition: A right or legal principle is stretched past its meaning, inverted, or applied to one side only, and a conclusion rests on that reading; the harm excused or the right denied must be one the law, or the entry's limits, names. The finding is about how the term is used in the text, not about the author.
detectors: The text names a right or principle and states a holder, a duty-bearer or a limit that differs from the glossary entry (for example a rule that binds the state is said to bind the press)
A conclusion about what someone may or may not do rests on that reading
A right is invoked to excuse a harm the law or the entry's limits names, or protection is invoked to deny someone a lawful right (both directions count)
The same right is invoked for one side and denied to the other in like circumstances
techniques.not_this: A genuine conflict between two rights, argued with both named; a strongly argued position that uses the term in its established sense; a quoted opponent's use of the term.

routing.attributed-motive: the text says why someone invokes the right (motive, no contradiction of the term)
routing.hasty-generalization: the misreading is pinned on a whole group
routing.Questioning_the_Reputation: the person's credibility, not the term, is attacked
routing.one-sided balancing: not a technique: only one of two paired rights is named and nothing contradicts the term, so it is a glossary note

techniques.name: Delegitimizing an opinion
techniques.definition: A view, or its holder (any person or group), is presented as not entitled to be voiced (illegitimate, evil, to be silenced), with no finding by a court, or by a body with legal power to decide it, cited; a cited finding is itself a claim to check. The finding is about the wording, not about anyone's purpose.
detectors: The text says a view must not be said, or that its holder has no right to say it, without arguing against the view
The view is called evil or illegitimate AND its holder is said to have no right to voice it, or should be silenced or excluded
A group is told to be silent because of what it believes (applies equally to every political side and to any group)
A person's standing to speak (office, role, parenthood) is denied because of the opinion
techniques.not_this: Moral condemnation that leaves the right to speak intact; a limit on speech that a court has found; calls for political accountability; satire; criticism of an official's use of office; arguing that a view is wrong with reasons; a rule of procedure that really limits who may speak at a given moment.

routing.attributed-motive: the text claims to know why someone holds the view (m15)
routing.hasty-generalization: all holders of the view are said to share it or the fault (m16)
routing.Name_Calling-Labeling: the label is the whole act, with no claim that the view may not be voiced (m17 nearest in switch)
routing.Questioning_the_Reputation: the person's credibility, not the standing of the view, is the target (m04)
